13319-the-return-of-peter-grimm:
David Belasco's stage play centres on Peter Grimm, an older man surrounded by family, a doctor, and a household full of unfinished business. Frederik, James, and Dr. MacPherson move through scenes of farewell, warning, and sharp talk about money, duty, and the future of the Grimm house.

The action turns on what Peter knows and what others hope to hide, with a storm-night telephone scene that gives the play its uncanny edge. Belasco, praised in the prefatory pages for painstaking stage realism, builds the drama from close domestic detail rather than spectacle. The result is a family reckoning played out in a single, closely watched home.
19068-household-stories-by-the-brothers-:
Lucy Crane translated these Household Stories from the Brothers Grimm, with pictures by Walter Crane. This Dover edition republishes the 1886 Macmillan text in full, including Sleeping Beauty, whose tower scene fronts the book. The tales come from German folk tradition.

Six men with strange powers face a king who locks them in a heated iron room, but the man with the little hat brings frost that freezes food in the dishes. The king's wrath grows as each plot fails. Young readers get classic fairy tales of wit, magic, and justice, told in clear, old-style English.
19911-the-practical-values-of-space-expl:
The Practical Values of Space Exploration is a United States congressional report. It comes from the House Committee on Science and Astronautics. Its staff pages list special counsel, consultants, and clerks by name. Philip B. Yeager served as special consultant. John A. Carstarphen Junior was chief clerk. The report dates from the early space race, about 1960. Sputnik had pushed Congress to justify space spending.

Committees had to translate rockets into practical public value. Weather, communication, and science benefits fill such reports. This one preserves the official case at the program's dawn. Its staff lists show how Congress built space expertise. The document is a baseline for American space policy history.
5314-household-tales-by-brothers-grimm:
Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm's Household Tales, translated by Margaret Hunt, gathers the famous fairy tales in their classic form. Its contents open with The Frog King, or Iron Henry, Cat and Mouse in Partnership, Our Lady's Child. The youth who went forth to learn what fear was comes next, followed by the wolf and the seven young kids and Faithful John.

Hunt's translation keeps the German titles alongside the English, and the collection runs through the twelve brothers, the pack of ragamuffins, and many more. Readers get the Grimms' tales as scholars collected them, darker and stranger than later retellings, and still the foundation of Western fairy tale.
55867-the-life-and-adventures-of-rear-ad:
The Life and Adventures of Rear-Admiral John Paul Jones is a biography by Abbott, published in New York in 1874. Abbott tells the life of the naval hero of the American Revolution, commonly called Paul Jones, and illustrates the volume with scenes such as the attack on Whitehaven.

In his preface Abbott confesses a conversion. He began, he says, believing Jones a reckless adventurer whose only merit was desperate daring. Study of Jones's words and deeds convinced him the man ranked with Washington, Jefferson, Franklin and Lafayette. Because that verdict runs against the current literature, Abbott promises to sustain every statement with documentary evidence, faults admitted, and the book argues its case like a brief for the defence.
58525-remarks-on-the-uses-of-some-of-the:
Remarks on the Uses of Some of the Bazaar Medicines is a medical handbook by Edward John Waring. Waring was a retired surgeon-major of the Indian army. He also edited the Pharmacopoeia of India. The fifth edition came out in London in 1897. A full index of diseases guides the reader to treatments.

The book covers common medical plants of India. It adds directions for drowning and snake-bites. Its prefaces tell the book's history. The fourth edition had sold out in India. Waring's son prepared the fifth with help from a family friend. New matter includes notes on the clinical thermometer. It also includes a fuller treatment of smallpox with carbolised oil.
59508-index-of-the-project-gutenberg-wor:
David Widger compiled an Index of the Project Gutenberg Works of Jacob Grimm and Wilhelm Grimm. The index gathers the tables of contents of the Grimm volumes held by Project Gutenberg. Sets listed include The Brothers Grimm Fairy Tales, Grimm Fairy Tales, Household Tales, Household Stories, Grimm Fairy Stories, and Snowdrop and Other Tales. Each set contents stands in full.

The Brothers Grimm Fairy Tales list opens with The Golden Bird, Hans in Luck, and Jorinda and Jorindel. The Travelling Musicians, Old Sultan, and The Straw, the Coal, and the Bean follow. Briar Rose, The Twelve Dancing Princesses, and The Fisherman and His Wife fill the early pages. The Frog Prince, Cat and Mouse in Partnership, The Goose Girl, and Rapunzel follow. Hansel and Gretel, Mother Holle, Little Red Cap, and Rumpelstiltskin close the sample. Readers get a map of every Grimm tale in the Gutenberg set.
69351-lectures-on-the-constitution-and-l:
Francis Stoughton Sullivan, professor of common law at the University of Dublin, wrote these Lectures on the Constitution and Laws of England. This second edition came out at London in 1776, with a discourse on the laws and government of England by Gilbert Stuart set before it. The book is dedicated to Lord North, then head of the government.

Sullivan's lectures carry a commentary on Magna Carta, the great charter of English liberty. They also illustrate many English statutes, showing how the law grew case by case. Stuart's added authorities and opening discourse frame the whole. The work belongs to the great age of English legal writing, when men like Blackstone were mapping the constitution for students and gentlemen alike. Sullivan's lectures were read in Ireland and America as well as at home.
doe-osti-2571209-stable-diacid-coordinat:
A Los Alamos National Laboratory final report under ARPA-E award DE-AR0001003, led by Yu Seung Kim and dated December 5, 2023, covers a new membrane for vehicle fuel cells. Today's automotive fuel cells use sulfonated polymer membranes and struggle to run above 100 degrees Celsius without added humidity. The project built membranes from quaternary ammonium polymers coordinated with diacids, designed for dry running across 80 to 230 degrees.

Running dry removes external humidifiers and demisters and lets radiators shrink, which simplifies the whole fuel cell system. The ion-pair design also tolerates impurities better and speeds catalyst reactions at the electrodes. Work ran from July 2019 to January 2023. The report closes by comparing system cost and feasibility against current fuel cells, and it ties the scale-up path to the DOE L'Innovator project on manufacturing the membrane at volume.
doe-osti-3374169-ier-620-ced-3b-experime:
Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory report IER-620 CED-3b, by R. Araj and dated April 2026, sums up the execution of pulsed-neutron die-away experiments with two moderating targets, propylene glycol and Mobilmet 423. In this method a burst of neutrons enters a target and the rate at which the neutron signal dies away reveals how the material slows and absorbs them. Such data support nuclear criticality safety and detector work.

The report describes the testbed, its detectors and electronics, and how targets and detectors were placed in the experiment room. Long tables record the measured counts run by run, with the raw timing data filling much of the document's 69 pages. As an execution summary, its job is to fix the setup and the data on record so later analysis can be traced back to exactly what was run.
household-stories-by-the-brothers-grimm:
Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected these household tales in Germany. Lucy Crane translated them into English, and Walter Crane drew the pictures. The hosted copy is Dover's 1963 reprint of the Macmillan edition of 1886. Sleeping Beauty, as Rosamond in the tower, fronts the book.

The Rabbit's Bride, Clever Grethel, and Six Soldiers of Fortune lead the list. Robbers flee a house of horrors in one famed tale retold here. Walter Crane's headpieces and tailpieces dress every story. The translations keep the tales' plain, brisk voice. Families have read this Crane edition for well over a century as a first Grimm.
household-tales-by-brothers-grimm:
Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm's Household Tales, in Margaret Hunt's translation, opens with The Frog King, or Iron Henry. Cat and Mouse in Partnership and Our Lady's Child follow in the contents. The Youth Who Went Forth to Learn What Fear Was takes fourth place. Two hundred tales stand in the full collection.

Rapunzel, Hansel and Gretel, Cinderella, and Little Red-Cap appear under their English names, each with its German title beside it. The Bremen Town Musicians sing, the elves work, and Godfather Death keeps his bargain. Hunt translated from the Grimms' final edition, the standard Victorian Englishing. These are the tales as the brothers printed them at last: harsher, stranger, and funnier than nursery retellings. Witches eat, children outwit, and justice arrives with an axe. The household book of Germany became, in this translation, the household book of the English-speaking nursery.
podcast-joerogan-avY3bV5yxMM:
Rachel Wilson takes the Rogan mic for episode 2460 of the Joe Rogan Experience, in a wide-ranging full-length talk. The episode is kept whole, so her views and stories arrive at her own pace rather than in clips chosen by others.

Across the sitting she holds forth on her ground, and Rogan draws her out in the show's open style. The transcript preserves the entire back-and-forth as aired. The entry serves listeners who want the complete appearance on file, a full record of one guest's hours in the chair, ready to be read or heard end to end.
the-return-of-peter-grimm:
An editor introduces David Belasco, born at San Francisco on July 25, 1853, as the Edison of the American stage. Belasco is praised as a creator with his own workshop, unlike contemporary managers described as manufacturers of amusement goods.

The portrait stresses his love of theatre, his willingness to take infinite pains for effect regardless of cost, and his skill at atmosphere and unified production. Only Winthrop Ames is said to rival his personal care. Readers meet the play through its producer's reputation, as a craftsman-manager carrying forward an older theatrical banner with new inventions.
